evidence.note: The one good sequence in the match: climb at t9 pays off with 'Hitman snaps off missile dropkick — Hall takes 19 damage', momentum 5-2, Hall GROUNDED. This is the only offensive spike the player produces all match.

Real trade-off offered and passed on: menu shows 'Cover — pinfall attempt', 'Sharpshooter 83% — cash in momentum for a match-ending swing', 'Leg drop 86%' and 'Pull opponent up'. The player takes pickup for 3 damage; from here Hall never drops below 109 HP again.

Dead loop: collar_elbow is 17 of 25 player turns (68.00%, exactly the reported move_repetition_rate) and is chosen on 14 consecutive player turns from t15 through t41. Health is frozen at [109, 109] from t20 to t28 while the tie-up/break cycle repeats.
Player HP falls 132 -> 83 across the loop while Hall stays at 109 from t13 to the final bell — 37 turns in which the player deals zero damage. That is a one-sided snowball with no comeback window.
50 turns (gate fail, band [8, 40]) and near_fall_count 0; the match ends on a 1-2-3 the player had no chance to break up after two unanswered Razor's Edges.

Loop-tax feedback is legible and escalating: the tie-up note changes from 'enter a tie-up to unlock throws and whips; repeat loops lose steam' (t1) to 'tie-up is going stale — pay it off or reset before they steal momentum' (t5), and the log confirms the cost — 'The repeated tie-up stalls out — Hall gains escape momentum.'
The cost is also visible numerically: the Collar-and-elbow label decays 91% (t15) -> 84% -> 78% -> 71% -> 65% -> 58% -> 57%, so a reader can see the move getting worse the more it is used.

But the menu contradicts its own warning: on every single stale turn Collar-and-elbow is still index 1 and still ties the best hit chance on offer (57% vs Straight right 57%, Roundhouse kick 52%). The text says reset while the ordering and the odds both say keep tying up.

Ambiguity in the groggy menu: 'Shake the cobwebs 61%' and 'Desperation strike 57%' carry the identical note 'clear the haze before they punish you' despite one being pure recovery and the other a strike attempt.

Status feedback is otherwise strong: 'Hitman is rattled — when they're forced up, big payoffs may open.' plus '— FINISHER — the next cover packs extra heat.' clearly telegraphs the incoming pin, and groggy reads as a modifier at t47 ('Hitman rises — still groggy from the impact!', position STANDING).
Pin visible when legal (curation_pin_visible true), and Sharpshooter 83% is framed as 'cash in momentum for a match-ending swing' — apply-the-hold odds, not a win probability.

Nothing new is discovered after t13: turns 15-41 are the same tie-up/break exchange, and the log alternates between two sentences ('The repeated tie-up stalls out…' 11 times, 'Hall uses the stale tie-up to reset with momentum' 7 times).
The ending removes agency rather than creating curiosity — two identical Razor's Edges at t46 and t48 with the player's only legal move being 'Fight to your feet' at 46% then 44%.
The single hook for a rematch is the unexplored fork at t13, where Sharpshooter at 83% and a Cover were both live with Hall grounded and rattled.

stickiness.rematch_reason: Only one specific question is left open — whether taking the Sharpshooter or the cover at t13 converts the missile-dropkick knockdown — because everything after that turn was the same tie-up exchange with no damage on either side.
stickiness.next_experiment: Re-run seed 206 with a policy that takes the Finish options at t13 (Sharpshooter 83% or Cover) and, whenever the note reads 'tie-up is going stale', switches to Straight right or a grapple payoff (Arm drag / Side headlock) instead of re-tying, to test whether the loop tax is actually escapable in play.

evidence.note: One clean impact beat: 'Hitman snaps off missile dropkick — Hall takes 19 damage' with Hall dropped to GROUNDED and momentum jumping to 5-2.
Feedback density collapses mid-match: turns 17-41 are almost entirely two alternating sentences, and log_uniqueness_ratio is 0.4844 with position_diversity only 7 — the ring never changes shape.

The Razor's Edge beat is well built: 'Hall snaps off razor's edge — Hitman takes 20 damage. Hitman is rattled… — FINISHER — the next cover packs extra heat.' State shifts to GROUNDED, and the promise is paid off at t50 with 'The finisher still echoes — +12 on the cover!'

Pin sequence is properly staged (delays 0.0 / 1.0 / 1.5 / 0.0 / 0.0) through 'Referee: 1… 2… 3!', but with near_fall_count 0 the three-count carries no doubt — there was never a kickout in the match to make the count feel dangerous.

top_issues.summary: The loop persists despite the warnings. Collar-and-elbow is chosen on 14 consecutive player turns (t15-t41) and 68% of all player turns; 'The repeated tie-up stalls out' fires 11 times and 'Hall uses the stale tie-up to reset with momentum' 7 times, yet nothing in the game state or the menu forces a different choice. The loop tax drains momentum but does not break the loop.
top_issues.suggested_area: escalating loop tax — gate or remove the repeated move from curation after N stale uses

top_issues.summary: The curated menu fights its own advice: while the note reads 'tie-up is going stale — pay it off or reset before they steal momentum', Collar-and-elbow remains index 1 and ties the highest displayed hit chance on every stale turn (e.g. t31: tie-up 57%, punch 57%, kick 52%). A player following either the ordering or the percentages does exactly what the text warns against.
top_issues.suggested_area: curation ordering / hit-% presentation when a move is flagged stale

top_issues.summary: Fairness and pacing: Hall's HP is unchanged at 109 from t13 to the final bell while the player falls 132 -> 25, so 37 of 50 turns contain no player offense at all. Combined with near_fall_count 0 and the 50-turn gate fail, the match has no comeback structure.
top_issues.suggested_area: momentum floor / comeback pressure when one side has taken no damage for many turns

top_issues.summary: Both groggy-recovery options at t43 and t45 share the identical note 'clear the haze before they punish you' even though Shake the cobwebs is a pure recovery and Desperation strike also deals damage.
top_issues.suggested_area: distinct note text for shake_groggy vs desperation_strike
